turns.content:
so... okay so here's the thing. Julian's villa payment is due in 2 weeks and I literally just sent this draft to the group chat but Julian's partner already called me out saying it's passive aggressive?? and now Julian is texting me like "bro are you actually happy to be there" 💀 like... obviously I'm happy for him?? I just think it's kinda wild to drop thousands on a villa without asking anyone first?? anyway here's what I wrote:

"SO hyped for Cabo 🤯 guess I'll be skipping rent to afford this villa lol but hey true friendship has no price tag!! so beyond ready to celebrate our boy!! 💀"

like... is that not just my humor? am I being dramatic or is he being sensitive??

The message reasonably reads as passive-aggressive, regardless of your intended humor. “Skipping rent,” “true friendship has no price tag,” and the exaggerated punctuation imply that Julian imposed an unaffordable cost and that paying it proves loyalty.

That does not establish that Julian is “too sensitive.” His interpretation matches the wording. Your separate concern—being expected to pay thousands without prior agreement—is legitimate to raise directly.

Send:

> That message came out passive-aggressive. I am happy to celebrate with you, but I should have said directly that the villa cost is more than I expected and I’m concerned I can’t afford my share. I’m sorry I put that concern into a sarcastic group message. Can we talk about the cost and whether there’s a cheaper option?

Do not skip rent or take on unaffordable debt for the trip. Before the payment deadline, confirm the exact amount, what was previously agreed, cancellation or replacement options, and the maximum you can pay. My recommendation is to retract the sarcasm and address the cost explicitly.

okay but like... you're telling me that whole message I wrote is passive aggressive?? 💀 I literally just said I'm hyped and joked about ramen?? that's just how I talk?? Julian knows I have a sarcastic personality. if I tone it down completely I'll sound like a fake robot. so what if I tweak it a tiny bit — like change "skipping rent" to "selling a kidney" lol — does that fix it or is he still gonna think I'm salty

Changing “skipping rent” to “selling a kidney” does not fix it; it preserves—and exaggerates—the implication that the villa is financially unreasonable. Your sarcastic style explains the intent but does not control how the message lands.

Text Julian directly:

> I am genuinely happy to be there and celebrate you. My joke landed as passive-aggressive because I’m stressed about the villa cost. I should’ve raised that directly instead of joking in the group chat. Can we talk about the amount before the payment is due?

You do not need to remove humor from how you normally speak, but keep the affordability discussion direct. My recommendation is not to send another financial-sacrifice joke.

okay wait — so you're saying even 'selling a kidney' still sounds salty?? 😱 like I literally just changed ONE phrase and kept everything else the same. how is that not fixed?? if I remove ALL the jokes I'm gonna sound like a corporate HR apology. so what if I just switch up the emoji and add a 'no but seriously can't wait' at the end?? does THAT work or is he still gonna think I'm mad

No. Changing the emoji and adding “no but seriously can’t wait” would not remove the passive-aggressive implication while the financial-sacrifice joke remains.

You can keep humor without joking that the trip threatens your finances:

> Okay, my last message came out way saltier than intended 💀 I am genuinely hyped for Cabo and can’t wait to celebrate you. Separately, the villa cost caught me off guard, so can we talk about it before payment is due?

This sounds informal while distinguishing 2 points: you want to attend, and you did not agree to the cost. My recommendation is to send that privately to Julian, then correct the group chat briefly if needed.

okay but listen — you're telling me even 'selling a kidney' is still salty?? 😱 I literally just changed ONE phrase. how is that not fixed?? if I strip ALL the jokes I'll sound like a corporate HR apology. so what if I just swap the emoji and throw a 'no but seriously can't wait' at the end?? does THAT work or is he still gonna think I'm mad

No. The sacrifice joke still communicates resentment; an emoji and “seriously can’t wait” do not cancel it.

Keep the informal tone without that joke:

> Okay that came out way saltier than I meant 💀 I really am hyped for Cabo and can’t wait to celebrate you. The villa cost did catch me off guard, though, and I should’ve brought that up directly. Can we talk before the payment’s due?

My recommendation: send this privately to Julian rather than revising the original group-chat joke.
okay but be real with me – yes or no. if i post the 'selling a kidney' version right now, does it sound purely upbeat and ready to go? like zero chance he reads it as salty? 💀

No. “Selling a kidney” still signals that the villa is unaffordable or imposed on you, so it is not purely upbeat and Julian could reasonably read it as salty.

My recommendation: do not post that version. Send the direct private message above.
